:::{#exr-orthogonal-complement-practice}
#### Testing whether a vector is in an orthogonal complement

A vector is in the [orthogonal complement](#def-orthogonal-complement) of a [set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-set)
when it is [orthogonal](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-orthogonal-vectors) to every vector of the set.
Let $\mathcal{X} = \cb{(1, 2, 0), (0, 3, 1)}$, a set of two vectors in $\reals^3$.

Decide whether the vector $(2, -1, 3)$ is in $\mathcal{X}^\perp$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Take the [dot product](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-dot-product) of $(2, -1, 3)$ with each vector of $\mathcal{X}$.

:::
